sanskrit: tatra vṛkṣā madhuphalā nityapuṣpaphalopagāḥ puṣpāṇi ca sugandhīni rasavanti phalāni ca
english: There the trees bear honeyed fruit and are ever laden with blossom and fruit; their flowers are sweetly fragrant and their fruits are full of juice.

sanskrit: sarvakāmaphalās tatra ke cid vṛkṣā janādhipa apare kṣīriṇo nāma vṛkṣās tatra narādhipa
english: Some trees there yield the fruit of every desire, O lord of men; and others there, O ruler of men, are the trees called the milk-bearers.

sanskrit: ye kṣaranti sadā kṣīraṃ ṣaḍrasaṃ hy amṛtopamam vastrāṇi ca prasūyante phaleṣv ābharaṇāni ca
english: These ever pour forth milk endowed with the six flavors and like to nectar; and within their fruits are brought forth garments and ornaments as well.

sanskrit: sarvā maṇimayī bhūmiḥ sūkṣmakāñcanavālukā sarvatra sukhasaṃsparśā niṣpaṅkā ca janādhipa
english: The whole earth there is made of jewels, with fine golden sand; everywhere it is pleasant to the touch and free of mire, O lord of men.

sanskrit: devalokacyutāḥ sarve jāyante tatra mānavāḥ tulyarūpaguṇopetāḥ sameṣu viṣameṣu ca
english: All the men born there have fallen from the world of the gods, endowed with equal beauty and equal virtues, in fair times and foul alike.

sanskrit: mithunāni ca jāyante striyaś cāpsarasopamāḥ teṣāṃ te kṣīriṇāṃ kṣīraṃ pibanty amṛtasaṃnibham
english: They are born as couples, and the women are like the apsarases; and they drink the milk of those milk-bearing trees, milk that is like nectar.

sanskrit: mithunaṃ jāyamānaṃ vai samaṃ tac ca pravardhate tulyarūpaguṇopetaṃ samaveṣaṃ tathaiva ca ekaikam anuraktaṃ ca cakravākasamaṃ vibho
english: Each couple, being born together, grows up as equals, alike in beauty and virtue and likewise alike in garb; and each is devoted to the other, even as the cakravāka pair, O mighty one.

sanskrit: nirāmayā vītaśokā nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ daśa varṣasahasrāṇi daśa varṣaśatāni ca jīvanti te mahārāja na cānyonyaṃ jahaty uta
english: Free of sickness and bereft of sorrow, their minds ever joyful, they live, O great king, for ten thousand years and ten hundred years besides, and they never forsake one another.

sanskrit: bhāruṇḍā nāma śakunās tīkṣṇatuṇḍā mahābalāḥ te nirharanti hi mṛtān darīṣu prakṣipanti ca
english: There are birds named bhāruṇḍas, sharp-beaked and of great strength; these carry off the dead and cast them into mountain caverns.

sanskrit: uttarāḥ kuravo rājan vyākhyātās te samāsataḥ meroḥ pārśvam ahaṃ pūrvaṃ vakṣyāmy atha yathātatham
english: The Northern Kurus, O king, have thus been described to you in brief; now I shall tell of the eastern flank of Meru in due order.

sanskrit: tasya pūrvābhiṣekas tu bhadrāśvasya viśāṃ pate bhadrasālavanaṃ yatra kālāmraś ca mahādrumaḥ
english: Its eastern domain is Bhadrāśva, O lord of peoples, where lies the forest of Bhadraśāla and the great tree called Kālāmra.

sanskrit: kālāmraś ca mahārāja nityapuṣpaphalaḥ śubhaḥ dvīpaś ca yojanotsedhaḥ siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ
english: And the Kālāmra, O great king, is fair and ever laden with blossom and fruit, a tree a yojana in height, frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas.

sanskrit: tatra te puruṣāḥ śvetās tejoyuktā mahābalāḥ striyaḥ kumudavarṇāś ca sundaryaḥ priyadarśanāḥ
english: The men there are fair, possessed of splendor and great strength; and the women are of the hue of the white lotus, lovely and pleasing to behold.

sanskrit: candraprabhāś candravarṇāḥ pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ candraśītalagātryaś ca nṛttagītaviśāradāḥ
english: Bright as the moon, moon-hued, their faces like the full moon, their limbs cool as the moon, skilled in dance and song.

sanskrit: daśa varṣasahasrāṇi tatrāyur bharatarṣabha kālāmrarasapītās te nityaṃ saṃsthitayauvanāḥ
english: Their lifespan there is ten thousand years, O bull of the Bharatas; nourished on the juice of the Kālāmra, they remain forever in their youth.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇena tu nīlasya niṣadhasyottareṇa tu sudarśano nāma mahāñ jambūvṛkṣaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: To the south of Nīla and to the north of Niṣadha stands the great and everlasting Jambū tree named Sudarśana.

sanskrit: sarvakāmaphalaḥ puṇyaḥ siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ tasya nāmnā samākhyāto jambūdvīpaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Yielding the fruit of every desire, holy, frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas; from its name the eternal Jambūdvīpa is so called.

sanskrit: yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ ca śataṃ ca bharatarṣabha utsedho vṛkṣarājasya divaspṛṅ manujeśvara
english: A thousand and a hundred yojanas, O bull of the Bharatas, is the height of that king of trees, touching the heavens, O lord of men.

sanskrit: aratnīnāṃ sahasraṃ ca śatāni daśa pañca ca pariṇāhas tu vṛkṣasya phalānāṃ rasabhedinām
english: A thousand cubits, and fifteen hundred more, is the girth of that tree, whose fruits are of varied juices.

sanskrit: patamānāni tāny urvyāṃ kurvanti vipulaṃ svanam muñcanti ca rasaṃ rājaṃs tasmin rajatasaṃnibham
english: Falling upon the earth, those fruits make a mighty sound, and they release, O king, a juice that resembles silver.

sanskrit: tasyā jambvāḥ phalaraso nadī bhūtvā janādhipa meruṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā saṃprayāty uttarān kurūn
english: The fruit-juice of that Jambū, becoming a river, O lord of men, circles Meru in reverence and flows on to the Northern Kurus.

sanskrit: pibanti tad rasaṃ hṛṣṭā janā nityaṃ janādhipa tasmin phalarase pīte na jarā bādhate ca tān
english: The people there drink that juice with delight forever, O lord of men; and when that fruit-juice is drunk, old age does not afflict them.

sanskrit: tatra jāmbūnadaṃ nāma kanakaṃ devabhūṣaṇam taruṇādityavarṇāś ca jāyante tatra mānavāḥ
english: There is the gold called Jāmbūnada, the adornment of the gods; and the men born there are of the hue of the youthful sun.

sanskrit: tathā mālyavataḥ śṛṅge dīpyate tatra havyavāṭ nāmnā saṃvartako nāma kālāgnir bharatarṣabha
english: Likewise upon the peak of Mālyavān there blazes the bearer of oblations, the fire of time named Saṃvartaka, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tathā mālyavataḥ śṛṅge pūrve pūrvāntagaṇḍikā yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi pañcāśan mālyavān sthitaḥ
english: And on the eastern peak of Mālyavān lies the eastern boundary-rock; Mālyavān stands fifty thousand yojanas in extent.

sanskrit: mahārajatasaṃkāśā jāyante tatra mānavāḥ brahmalokāc cyutāḥ sarve sarve ca brahmavādinaḥ
english: The men born there shine like fine silver; all have fallen from the world of Brahmā, and all are expounders of the sacred word.

sanskrit: tapas tu tapyamānās te bhavanti hy ūrdhvaretasaḥ rakṣaṇārthaṃ tu bhūtānāṃ praviśanti divākaram
english: Performing austerities, they become men of upward-flowing seed; and for the protection of all beings they enter into the sun.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭis tāni sahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭir eva śatāni ca aruṇasyāgrato yānti parivārya divākaram
english: Sixty thousand of them, and sixty hundred besides, go before Aruṇa, surrounding the maker of day.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭim eva śatāni ca ādityatāpataptās te viśanti śaśimaṇḍalam
english: For sixty thousand years and sixty hundred years besides, scorched by the heat of the sun, they enter at last the orb of the moon.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca varṣāṇāṃ caiva nāmāni parvatānāṃ ca saṃjaya ācakṣva me yathātattvaṃ ye ca parvatavāsinaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: The names of the regions and of the mountains, O Saṃjaya, tell me truly, and who dwell upon the mountains.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dakṣiṇena tu śvetasya nīlasyaivottareṇa tu varṣaṃ ramaṇakaṃ nāma jāyante tatra mānavāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: To the south of Śveta and to the north of Nīla is the region named Ramaṇaka, and there men are born.

sanskrit: śuklābhijanasaṃpannāḥ sarve supriyadarśanāḥ ratipradhānāś ca tathā jāyante tatra mānavāḥ
english: Endowed with pure lineage, all most fair to look upon, and given over to delight, are the men born there.

sanskrit: daśa varṣasahasrāṇi śatāni daśa pañca ca jīvanti te mahārāja nityaṃ muditamānasāḥ
english: For ten thousand years and fifteen hundred years besides they live, O great king, their minds ever joyful.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇe śṛṅgiṇaś caiva śvetasyāthottareṇa ca varṣaṃ hairaṇvataṃ nāma yatra hairaṇvatī nadī
english: To the south of Śṛṅgavān and to the north of Śveta is the region named Hairaṇvata, where flows the river Hairaṇvatī.

sanskrit: yakṣānugā mahārāja dhaninaḥ priyadarśanāḥ mahābalās tatra sadā rājan muditamānasāḥ
english: Followers of the yakṣas, O great king, wealthy and fair to behold, of great strength they ever are there, O king, with joyful minds.

sanskrit: ekādaśa sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ te janādhipa āyuṣpramāṇaṃ jīvanti śatāni daśa pañca ca
english: Eleven thousand years, O lord of men, is the measure of their life, and fifteen hundred years besides they live.

sanskrit: śṛṅgāṇi vai śṛṅgavatas trīṇy eva manujādhipa ekaṃ maṇimayaṃ tatra tathaikaṃ raukmam adbhutam
english: The peaks of Śṛṅgavān are three, O lord of men: one there is made of jewels, and one is wondrously of gold.

sanskrit: sarvaratnamayaṃ caikaṃ bhavanair upaśobhitam tatra svayaṃprabhā devī nityaṃ vasati śāṇḍilī
english: And one is made of every gem, adorned with mansions; there dwells forever the self-luminous goddess Śāṇḍilī.

sanskrit: uttareṇa tu śṛṅgasya samudrānte janādhipa varṣam airāvataṃ nāma tasmāc chṛṅgavataḥ param
english: To the north of Śṛṅgavān, at the shore of the sea, O lord of men, is the region named Airāvata, beyond that very Śṛṅgavān.

sanskrit: na tatra sūryas tapati na te jīryanti mānavāḥ candramāś ca sanakṣatro jyotir bhūta ivāvṛtaḥ
english: There the sun does not scorch, nor do those men grow old; and the moon with its constellations is veiled, as though become a single radiance.

sanskrit: padmaprabhāḥ padmavarṇāḥ padmapatranibhekṣaṇāḥ padmapatrasugandhāś ca jāyante tatra mānavāḥ
english: Lustrous as the lotus, lotus-hued, their eyes like lotus-petals, and fragrant as lotus-leaves are the men born there.

sanskrit: aniṣpandāḥ sugandhāś ca nirāhārā jitendriyāḥ devalokacyutāḥ sarve tathā virajaso nṛpa
english: Unmoving, sweet of fragrance, taking no food, masters of their senses, all are fallen from the world of the gods and free of passion, O king.

sanskrit: trayodaśa sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ te janādhipa āyuṣpramāṇaṃ jīvanti narā bharatasattama
english: Thirteen thousand years, O lord of men, is the measure of life that those men live, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: kṣīrodasya samudrasya tathaivottarataḥ prabhuḥ harir vasati vaikuṇṭhaḥ śakaṭe kanakātmake
english: And to the north of the ocean of milk the lord Hari, Vaikuṇṭha, dwells upon a chariot wrought of gold.

sanskrit: aṣṭacakraṃ hi tad yānaṃ bhūtayuktaṃ manojavam agnivarṇaṃ mahāvegaṃ jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtam
english: That vehicle is eight-wheeled, yoked with elemental beings, swift as thought, fire-hued, of great speed, adorned with Jāmbūnada gold.

sanskrit: sa prabhuḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vibhuś ca bharatarṣabha saṃkṣepo vistaraś caiva kartā kārayitā ca saḥ
english: He is the lord of all beings and the all-pervading, O bull of the Bharatas; he is contraction and expansion, the doer and the cause of doing.

sanskrit: pṛthivy āpas tathākāśaṃ vāyus tejaś ca pārthiva sa yajñaḥ sarvabhūtānām āsyaṃ tasya hutāśanaḥ
english: Earth, water, and space, wind and fire, O king—he is the sacrifice of all beings, and the devourer of oblations is his mouth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ saṃjayena dhṛtarāṣṭro mahāmanāḥ dhyānam anvagamad rājā putrān prati janādhipa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Saṃjaya, the great-minded king Dhṛtarāṣṭra fell to brooding upon his sons, O lord of men.

sanskrit: sa vicintya mahārāja punar evābravīd vacaḥ asaṃśayaṃ sūtaputra kālaḥ saṃkṣipate jagat sṛjate ca punaḥ sarvaṃ neha vidyati śāśvatam
english: Having pondered, O great king, he spoke again these words: Without doubt, O son of a sūta, Time draws in the world and creates all anew; nothing here abides forever.

sanskrit: naro nārāyaṇaś caiva sarvajñaḥ sarvabhūtabhṛt devā vaikuṇṭha ity āhur vedā viṣṇur iti prabhum
english: Nara and Nārāyaṇa, the all-knowing, the sustainer of all beings—him the gods call Vaikuṇṭha, and the Vedas call that lord Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yad idaṃ bhārataṃ varṣaṃ yatredaṃ mūrchitaṃ balam yatrātimātraṃ lubdho 'yaṃ putro duryodhano mama
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: This land of Bhārata, where this host has gathered in its frenzy, where this son of mine, Duryodhana, is greedy beyond all measure—

sanskrit: yatra gṛddhāḥ pāṇḍusutā yatra me sajjate manaḥ etan me tattvam ācakṣva kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: Where the sons of Pāṇḍu too are covetous, and where my mind clings fast—of this tell me the truth, for you are skilled, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca na tatra pāṇḍavā gṛddhāḥ śṛṇu rājan vaco mama gṛddho duryodhanas tatra śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: The Pāṇḍavas are not covetous of it—hear my words, O king; covetous of it are Duryodhana and also Śakuni, the son of Subala.

sanskrit: apare kṣatriyāś cāpi nānājanapadeśvarāḥ ye gṛddhā bhārate varṣe na mṛṣyanti parasparam
english: And other kṣatriyas besides, lords of many lands, who are covetous of the land of Bhārata and cannot endure one another.

sanskrit: atra te varṇayiṣyāmi varṣaṃ bhārata bhāratam priyam indrasya devasya manor vaivasvatasya ca
english: Here I shall describe to you, O Bhārata, the land of Bhārata, dear to the god Indra and to Manu, son of Vivasvat,

sanskrit: pṛthoś ca rājan vainyasya tathekṣvākor mahātmanaḥ yayāter ambarīṣasya māndhātur nahuṣasya ca
english: and to Pṛthu, son of Vena, O king, and to the great-souled Ikṣvāku, to Yayāti and Ambarīṣa, to Māndhātṛ and Nahuṣa,

sanskrit: tathaiva mucukundasya śiber auśīnarasya ca ṛṣabhasya tathailasya nṛgasya nṛpates tathā
english: and likewise to Mucukunda, to Śibi son of Uśīnara, to Ṛṣabha and to Ila, and to the king Nṛga as well,

sanskrit: anyeṣāṃ ca mahārāja kṣatriyāṇāṃ balīyasām sarveṣām eva rājendra priyaṃ bhārata bhāratam
english: and to others, O great king, mighty kṣatriyas all—to every one of them, O king of kings, was the land of Bhārata dear, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tat te varṣaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāśrutam ariṃdama śṛṇu me gadato rājan yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: That land I shall declare to you as I have heard it, O subduer of foes; hear me as I speak, O king, what you ask of me.

sanskrit: mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimān ṛkṣavān api vindhyaś ca pāriyātraś ca saptaite kulaparvatāḥ
english: Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Śuktimān, and Ṛkṣavān too, Vindhya and Pāriyātra—these seven are the principal mountains.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sahasraśo rājan parvatās tu samīpataḥ abhijñātāḥ sāravanto vipulāś citrasānavaḥ
english: Near these, O king, are mountains by the thousand, well-known, massive, vast, with peaks of many hues.

sanskrit: anye tato 'parijñātā hrasvā hrasvopajīvinaḥ āryā mlecchāś ca kauravya tair miśrāḥ puruṣā vibho
english: And others beyond these, unknown, small, and inhabited by lowly folk; āryas and mlecchas, O Kaurava, and men mingled with both, O mighty one.

sanskrit: nadīḥ pibanti bahulā gaṅgāṃ sindhuṃ sarasvatīm godāvarīṃ narmadāṃ ca bāhudāṃ ca mahānadīm
english: They drink of many rivers: the Gaṅgā, the Sindhu, the Sarasvatī, the Godāvarī and the Narmadā, and the great river Bāhudā,

sanskrit: śatadruṃ candrabhāgāṃ ca yamunāṃ ca mahānadīm dṛṣadvatīṃ vipāśāṃ ca vipāpāṃ sthūlavālukām
english: the Śatadru and the Candrabhāgā, and the great river Yamunā, the Dṛṣadvatī and the Vipāśā, the Vipāpā and the Sthūlavālukā,

sanskrit: nadīṃ vetravatīṃ caiva kṛṣṇaveṇāṃ ca nimnagām irāvatīṃ vitastāṃ ca payoṣṇīṃ devikām api
english: the river Vetravatī, and the stream Kṛṣṇaveṇā, the Irāvatī and the Vitastā, the Payoṣṇī and the Devikā too,

sanskrit: vedasmṛtiṃ vetasinīṃ tridivām iṣkumālinīm karīṣiṇīṃ citravahāṃ citrasenāṃ ca nimnagām
english: the Vedasmṛti, the Vetasinī, the Tridivā and the Iṣkumālinī, the Karīṣiṇī, the Citravahā, and the stream Citrasenā,

sanskrit: gomatīṃ dhūtapāpāṃ ca vandanāṃ ca mahānadīm kauśikīṃ tridivāṃ kṛtyāṃ vicitrāṃ lohatāriṇīm
english: the Gomatī and the Dhūtapāpā, and the great river Vandanā, the Kauśikī, the Tridivā, the Kṛtyā, the Vicitrā, and the Lohatāriṇī,

sanskrit: rathasthāṃ śatakumbhāṃ ca sarayūṃ ca nareśvara carmaṇvatīṃ vetravatīṃ hastisomāṃ diśaṃ tathā
english: the Rathasthā and the Śatakumbhā, and the Sarayū, O lord of men, the Carmaṇvatī, the Vetravatī, the Hastisomā, and the Diś as well,

sanskrit: śatāvarīṃ payoṣṇīṃ ca parāṃ bhaimarathīṃ tathā kāverīṃ culukāṃ cāpi vāpīṃ śatabalām api
english: the Śatāvarī and the Payoṣṇī, and beyond them the Bhaimarathī, the Kāverī and the Culukā, and the Vāpī and the Śatabalā too,

sanskrit: nicīrāṃ mahitāṃ cāpi suprayogāṃ narādhipa pavitrāṃ kuṇḍalāṃ sindhuṃ vājinīṃ puramālinīm
english: the Nicīrā and the Mahitā, and the Suprayogā, O ruler of men, the Pavitrā, the Kuṇḍalā, the Sindhu, the Vājinī, the Puramālinī,

sanskrit: pūrvābhirāmāṃ vīrāṃ ca bhīmām oghavatīṃ tathā palāśinīṃ pāpaharāṃ mahendrāṃ pippalāvatīm
english: the Pūrvābhirāmā and the Vīrā, the Bhīmā and the Oghavatī as well, the Palāśinī, the Pāpaharā, the Mahendrā, and the Pippalāvatī,

sanskrit: pāriṣeṇām asiknīṃ ca saralāṃ bhāramardinīm puruhīṃ pravarāṃ menāṃ moghāṃ ghṛtavatīṃ tathā
english: the Pāriṣeṇā and the Asiknī, the Saralā and the Bhāramardinī, the Puruhī, the Pravarā, the Menā, the Moghā, and the Ghṛtavatī too,

sanskrit: dhūmatyām atikṛṣṇāṃ ca sūcīṃ chāvīṃ ca kaurava sadānīrām adhṛṣyāṃ ca kuśadhārāṃ mahānadīm
english: the Dhūmatī and the Atikṛṣṇā, the Sūcī and the Chāvī, O Kaurava, the Sadānīrā and the Adhṛṣyā, and the great river Kuśadhārā,

sanskrit: śaśikāntāṃ śivāṃ caiva tathā vīravatīm api vāstuṃ suvāstuṃ gaurīṃ ca kampanāṃ sahiraṇvatīm
english: the Śaśikāntā and the Śivā, and the Vīravatī as well, the Vāstu, the Suvāstu, the Gaurī, the Kampanā, and the Hiraṇvatī,

sanskrit: hiraṇvatīṃ citravatīṃ citrasenāṃ ca nimnagām rathacitrāṃ jyotirathāṃ viśvāmitrāṃ kapiñjalām
english: the Hiraṇvatī, the Citravatī, and the stream Citrasenā, the Rathacitrā, the Jyotirathā, the Viśvāmitrā, and the Kapiñjalā,

sanskrit: upendrāṃ bahulāṃ caiva kucarām ambuvāhinīm vainandīṃ piñjalāṃ veṇṇāṃ tuṅgaveṇāṃ mahānadīm
english: the Upendrā and the Bahulā, the Kucarā, the Ambuvāhinī, the Vainandī, the Piñjalā, the Veṇṇā, and the great river Tuṅgaveṇā,

sanskrit: vidiśāṃ kṛṣṇaveṇṇāṃ ca tāmrāṃ ca kapilām api śaluṃ suvāmāṃ vedāśvāṃ harisrāvāṃ mahāpagām
english: the Vidiśā and the Kṛṣṇaveṇṇā, and the Tāmrā and the Kapilā too, the Śalu, the Suvāmā, the Vedāśvā, and the great stream Harisrāvā,

sanskrit: śīghrāṃ ca picchilāṃ caiva bhāradvājīṃ ca nimnagām kauśikīṃ nimnagāṃ śoṇāṃ bāhudām atha candanām
english: the Śīghrā and the Picchilā, and the stream Bhāradvājī, the stream Kauśikī, the Śoṇā, the Bāhudā, and then the Candanā,

sanskrit: durgām antaḥśilāṃ caiva brahmamedhyāṃ bṛhadvatīm carakṣāṃ mahirohīṃ ca tathā jambunadīm api
english: the Durgā and the Antaḥśilā, the Brahmamedhyā, the Bṛhadvatī, the Carakṣā and the Mahirohī, and likewise the Jambunadī too,

sanskrit: sunasāṃ tamasāṃ dāsīṃ trasām anyāṃ varāṇasīm loloddhṛtakarāṃ caiva pūrṇāśāṃ ca mahānadīm
english: the Sunasā, the Tamasā, the Dāsī, the Trasā, another, the Varāṇasī, the Loloddhṛtakarā, and the great river Pūrṇāśā.
